QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_78

question.text: How do client-level position limits in single-stock equity derivatives differ from client-level limits in currency derivatives in India?

answer.text: For equity single-stock derivatives, the client-level gross open position limit in any single underlying is the higher of 1% of the free-float market capitalization of the stock or 5% of the open interest in derivatives on that underlying (per exchange). For currency derivatives, client-level limits are specified in notional USD-equivalent terms — for example, an FPI / eligible-user limit of USD 100 million equivalent in USDINR — with participant-specific gross open position caps
Both segments have identical position limits of 5% of total open interest
Currency derivatives have no client-level position limits since they are OTC-equivalent
Equity derivatives position limits are set by RBI while currency derivatives limits are set by SEBI

explanation.text: The Logic: The equity single-stock client-level limit is computed per underlying, per exchange, as the HIGHER of 1% of the stock's free-float market capitalisation or 5% of the open interest in derivatives on that underlying. The currency client-level framework is different: limits are specified in notional USD-equivalent terms — for example, USD 100 million equivalent for FPIs/eligible users in USDINR — with participant-category-specific gross open position caps. The Trap: The equity client-level limit is NOT the MWPL itself (MWPL is a market-wide cap of 20% of free-float shares) and is not a flat 5% of OI. Currency derivatives DO have client-level position limits. SEBI and RBI jointly determine the currency framework; SEBI alone is not the source. Note: Always check the per-underlying client cap separately from market-wide and trading-member-level caps. A client can comply with the MWPL/TM rules and still breach the client cap in a single underlying.
